---
title: "Small Budgets, Big Screams"
subtitle: "Why horror is the safest bet in Hollywood"
---

::: {.reel}
Feature Story
:::

::: {.stat-row}
::: {.stat .pure}
[Horror movies that earned 10x their budget]{.label}

[1 in 5]{.num}

[about 21% of 295 horror films]{.small}
:::

::: {.stat .mix}
[Comedies that earned 10x their budget]{.label}

[1 in 18]{.num}

[about 6% of 807 comedies]{.small}
:::
:::

```{r}
source("prep.R")

tiers <- movies |>
  filter(genre %in% c("Horror", "Comedy")) |>
  mutate(tier = cut(production_budget,
                    breaks = c(0, 5e6, 20e6, 50e6, Inf),
                    labels = c("Under $5M", "$5M to $20M", "$20M to $50M", "Over $50M"),
                    right = FALSE)) |>
  group_by(genre, tier) |>
  summarise(median_return = median(return_ratio), films = n(), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(tiers, aes(x = tier, y = median_return, fill = genre)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(median_return, 1), "x")),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), vjust = -0.5, size = 4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "#9ca3af") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = genre_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title = "Horror out-earns comedy at every budget level",
    subtitle = "Typical (median) worldwide box office divided by budget. The dashed line is breaking even.",
    x = "Production budget",
    y = "Times budget earned back",
    fill = NULL,
    caption = "Data: The Numbers, via TidyTuesday (807 comedies, 295 horror movies)"
  ) +
  theme_fear() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

::: {.dropcap}
Horror is cheap to make. The typical horror movie in this data cost about \$11 million, while the typical comedy cost about \$18 million. Yet horror earns back more at every budget level, and the gap is widest for the smallest films. A horror movie made for under \$5 million typically earned about 3.5 times its budget.
:::

::: {.pullquote}
One in five horror movies earned back ten times what it cost.
:::

The biggest success stories are almost all tiny productions. The top five horror movies by return were each made for about a million dollars or less:

```{r}
movies |>
  filter(genre == "Horror") |>
  slice_max(return_ratio, n = 5) |>
  transmute(
    Movie = movie,
    Year = year,
    Budget = dollar(production_budget),
    `Worldwide gross` = dollar(worldwide_gross),
    `Times budget` = paste0(round(return_ratio), "x")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.labnote}
[Lab Note]{.lab-label}

Why can fear be made so cheaply? Horror works mostly through **anticipation**: a dark hallway, a sound off screen, a door left open. The audience's own imagination fills in the threat, which costs nothing to film. *Paranormal Activity* and *The Blair Witch Project* barely show their monsters at all, and that is a big part of why they feel so frightening. Comedy, on the other hand, usually depends on well known stars and many scenes, which raises the price.
:::
